sounds.intro: Kyrgyz uses Cyrillic with three extra letters. There are no genders and no articles. The stress is usually on the last syllable. Learn the special letters first.
rows: say "oh" with rounded lips, like German "ö"
say "ee" with rounded lips, like German "ü"
a short, flat "uh", like the "a" in "about"
at the back of the mouth these are made further back, in back-vowel words
notes: Vowel harmony: back vowels (а, о, у, ы) and front vowels (э, и, ө, ү) are not mixed in one word. Suffixes follow the same rule.

grammar.title: Pronouns
text: Kyrgyz often drops the pronoun, because the verb ending shows who is speaking. There is no he / she difference: "ал" means both.

grammar.title: Singular and plural
text: Add -лар, -лер, -дар, -дер, -тар, -тер or -лор, -лөр, by vowel harmony and the last sound. After a number, the noun stays singular: эки китеп (two book).

grammar.title: To be: -мын, -сың, -быз
text: There is no separate verb "to be". Add an ending to the noun or adjective. The ending changes by vowel harmony and the last sound: -мын / -мин / -бын / -бин / -пын / -пин.

grammar.title: Bar and jok: have, there is
text: Kyrgyz says "at me there is" (бар) or "at me there is not" (жок). The ending -да / -де means "at" or "in".

grammar.title: Present tense
text: Verb stem + а / е / й + person ending. Келүү (to come): кел-е-м.

grammar.title: Basic sentences
text: The verb goes last. Order: who, where or when, what, verb. Kyrgyz has no articles: "китеп" means "a book" or "the book".

grammar.title: Negation
text: Put -ба / -бе / -па / -пе / -бо / -бө / -по / -пө after the verb stem: барам (I go), барбайм (I do not go). For nouns use "эмес" (is not). "Жок" means "there is not". Always compare with the positive form.
ex: I do not have a car
he does not work on Sundays

grammar.title: Asking questions
text: Add the little word -бы / -би / -бу / -бү / -пы / -пи after the word you are asking about. It is the same for every question.

grammar.title: Question words
text: Question words stand where the answer would stand.

grammar.title: Possessives and liking
text: Endings go on the noun: -ым / -им (my), -ың / -иң (your), -ы / -и (his / her). To say you like something, use "мага жагат" (to me it is pleasing).

grammar.title: Formal vs informal
text: сен (informal): friends, family, children. сиз (formal): strangers, older people, work. Verb endings change: -сың (informal), -сыз (formal).

grammar.title: Past and future (simple)
text: Past: -ды / -ди / -ты / -ти + person ending (бардым = I went). Future uses the present form with a time word: эртең барам (tomorrow I go).

grammar.title: Commands
text: Informal: the bare verb stem. Formal: add -ыңыз / -иңиз. To forbid, add -ба / -бе after the stem.

grammar.title: Can, must, want
text: Can: verb + а алуу (сүзө алам, I can swim). Must: "керек" (needed). Want: -гым келет (жегим келет, I want to eat).
ex: I do not want to eat

grammar.title: In, on, at
text: Kyrgyz uses endings, not words in front: -да / -де (in, on, at), -га / -ге (to), -дан / -ден (from), -дын / -дин (of).
ex: the book is on the table
the cat is under the table
the shop is next to the bank
the park is near the station
the key is in the bag

grammar.title: Comparing things
text: Add -ыраак / -ирээк to the adjective for "more": чоң, чоңураак. For "the most" put "эң" before it: эң чоң. "Than" is -дан / -ден.
